Those results will then be validated with experimental test results. The phase II effort involved the utilization of the knowledge learned in phase I to establish the quantitative correlation between the microstructure characteristics and the riveting performance, which will be further used to guide the optimization of HPDC Al alloy microstructure using heat treatment process to achieve sufficient rivetability to join large thin-wall HPDC alloys. 3. BENEFITS TO THE FUNDING DOE OFFICE’S MISSION The project will ensure accurate prediction of the microstructure effects on bendability and rivetability of super large die cast (SLDC) Al alloys, giving guidance to the process optimization of the SLDC process to reach the department of energy goal considerable vehicle light-weighting and cost-cutting and promote the EV adoption and substantial decarbonization. 4. TECHNICAL DISCUSSION OF THE WORK PERFORMED BY ALL PARTIES In order to most effectively and efficiently meet the project objectives outlined above, the team established a phase -I project plan with four tasks (1-3) with phase-II project plan with additional four tasks (4-7) 1) Alloy selection and microstructure characterizations 2) Tension, 3-point bending and clinch Test Specimen Manufacturing 3) Hierarchical macro-micro model development of three point bending and clinch test 4) Calibrate hierarchical macro-micro model to an AlSi7MgMn (Aural-5) HPDC Al alloys with multiple e-coating conditions 5) Validation of the model parameters using HPDC Aural-5 alloys with multiple casting conditions 4.1 Alloy selection and microstructure characterizations The high pressure diecast (HPDC) Al alloy (Aural-5: Al7SiMgMn) is selected for this work, with Si as the major alloy element with around 7 wt% concentration, Mg and Si as minor alloy elements with less than 1 wt% concentration. This alloy is highly castable and possess good combination of strength and ductility and is the prime focus at Ford Motor company for use in super-large HPDC of car front-end, back-end and underbody structures, providing potentials for significant weight and cost reduction for electric vehicles. In this study, the HPDC aural-5 plate with a thickness of 2.85 mm is used, both in as-cast (F temper) and e-coated condition (H81 temper). The microstructure characterization of the as-cast condition is mainly performed through the optical microscope with the magnification of 200x and 500x. Five images were taken for both magnifications for each of the two areas: near the edge or in the center. The typical recorded microstructures are shown in Fig. 1. As shown in the figure, there are two major features of the microstructures: (a) the primary Al dendrites and (b) the Al+Si eutectics. While small amount of porosity is in the microstructure near the edge, there are more porosity shown in the center. The light-colored phase is the primary Al dendrites and the grey region represent the Al+Si eutectics. The dark region represents pores in the microstructure.
